This is also when one pro's contrarian system produces his biggest perch of the year: late in the fall a heavy 3/4-oz football jig on the bottom in deep water. It's a big-lure exception to the small-bait rule, and it belongs to this season.

groups.label: How to fish it
lines: Search with a drifted crawler or spinner harness, anchor on the school, and slip-bobber them 6–12 in off bottom. After turnover, follow them deeper again — late-fall perch go back out to where the bait is.
Search with a drifted crawler or spinner harness, anchor on the school, and slip-bobber them 6–12 in off bottom. Follow them deeper again — late-fall perch go back out to where the bait is.

groups.label: If it's still tough
lines: If the staging areas are empty, there's no bait there — leave. Staging perch are bait-driven; find the shiner clouds and you've found the fish.

groups.label: What to tie on
lines: Small jigs and minnows, fished deep and slow — plus that deep football-jig option: a 3/4-oz jig worked right on the bottom in deep water is a legitimate late-fall jumbo bait, not a mistake.

groups.label: How to fish it
lines: Fish vertically over the school once sonar finds them, keep the bait within a foot of bottom, and move with the baitfish — cold-water perch don't stray far from the food.

groups.label: If it's still tough
lines: Small and still beats big and busy now. A deadsticked minnow at the base of deep structure is the late-fall percentage play.

groups.label: What to tie on
lines: Tiny tungsten teardrops — 3–4.5 mm, glow, black, chartreuse or orange — and small spoons. Tip with a whole minnow or a minnow head (the head alone is very productive), or maggots on the finesse rig.

groups.label: How to fish it
lines: Hole-hop: 5–10 minutes a hole, holes 50–75 ft apart, drilled in a C-pattern search. And work the bait close to bottom — perch root insect larvae out of it, and pounding the bottom draws them in.

groups.label: If it's still tough
lines: Minnows sort for size under the ice, too: waxworms catch smaller fish, so if you're sorting dinks, switch the tipping to a whole minnow or minnow head.

groups.label: What to tie on
lines: The three-rod system covers a school: a 3-in rattling darter-style bait as the aggressive rod, a 1/16- to 1/8-oz rattling spoon in the middle, and a slick jig pounding bottom as the third. Whole minnows near structure, waxworms and maggots out on the flats.

groups.label: How to fish it
lines: Fish the middle of the day like it's prime time — for winter jumbos, it is. Pound the bottom to pull rooting fish in, then let the bait sit in the cloud.

groups.label: If it's still tough
lines: The tough-bite rig is as small as it gets: a bead-chain dropper to a #6 or #8 tungsten jig with one or two maggots, jigged on the bottom with the line held tight to a tiny float, on 3–4 lb line. Beside it, a back-hooked minnow on a deadstick (#4 or #6 octopus hook) — about a 12-in leash when fish are neutral, 18–20 in when they're neutral but moving.

groups.label: What to tie on
lines: Small tungsten jigs with maggots over the mud, minnow and minnow-head rigs where you want size. Keep one rod aggressive (rattling spoon) and one rod still.

groups.label: How to fish it
lines: Follow the hatch edges — where gravel meets mud is the late-ice perch line. Hole-hop the transition until you land on a school, then set up on it properly.

groups.label: If it's still tough
lines: If the flats are dead, the hatch hasn't started there — slide toward the spawning shallows; late-ice perch are travelling one direction now.

movementSeasons.heading: Frai
lines: Perch spawn in the shallows in early spring, over weeds a few feet deep, and they're the first panfish to move in. South-facing coves and dark bottoms warm first — in one measured case the back of a south cove ran 4 °F warmer in 3 ft of water than the main lake. Docks, stumps and laydowns that soak up sun hold early fish.

movementSeasons.heading: Après-frai
lines: After the spawn, perch head back to shallow warming water first, then slide toward the deeper weedlines as things warm. Follow the weed growth — emerging grass in the shallows is holding the food, and the perch.
After the spawn, perch head back to shallow warming water first. Follow the weed growth — emerging grass in the shallows is holding the food, and the perch.

movementSeasons.heading: Été
lines: Summer perch live deeper: the deeper weedlines and offshore structure. For the jumbos, the key teaching is the base of the structure, not the top — they feed at the bottom-type transitions at a structure's foot, on ground surrounded by soft bottom, from mid-morning to early evening. Isolated rockpiles, reefs and hard-bottom humps are the spots.
At about 8–9 in a perch's diet shifts to minnows, and the jumbos follow them — the smallest shiners matter most to the biggest fish.

movementSeasons.heading: Automne
lines: From late summer through freeze-up, jumbos gather on the transitions from hard bottom to soft — 10 ft down in shallow inland lakes, 40 ft and more on the Great Lakes. Ahead of winter they stage on sand or rock with scattered weeds in 8–12 ft, close to soft mucky bottom — and clouds of baitfish are a must; no bait, no staging perch.

movementSeasons.heading: Fin d’automne
lines: Late-fall perch are out deep with the bait after turnover — main-basin structure bases and the deep side of the fall transitions. His biggest perch of the year came to one pro in 35 ft of water at this time, off the deep pattern.

movementSeasons.heading: Glace précoce
lines: Early ice: shallow backwaters, just 1½–8 ft, and the weed edges. Perch are the first panfish in during the fall and the first you'll find shallow under new ice.

movementSeasons.heading: Glace de mi-hiver
lines: Mid-winter, jumbos slide from the structure bases out onto the basin flats as insect eggs hatch into food. The midday hours are theirs: big winter perch feed roughly 9 to 3 at the base of structure — they need light coming through the ice, and they don't feed with the walleyes at dawn and dusk.

movementSeasons.heading: Glace tardive
lines: Late ice: mud flats and the sand-gravel edges of mud flats, where the insect and larvae hatches kick off — and the staging water on the way to the spawning shallows. Bait 1–2 ft off bottom over the mud is the standard late-ice depth.

movementDaily.heading: Open water
lines: Most active at dusk; quietest at after dark.

movementDaily.heading: Through the ice
lines: Most active at midday; quietest at after dark.

weatherFacts: Feeding peaks in water 20–21 °C — the top of this species' temperature curve in the rating model.
Upper lethal temperature: about 32.3 °C, from the species' research file.

weatherOverlays.heading: Le lendemain d’un front
lines: One honest note: no perch book or study we found gives perch a barometric-pressure rule, so there's no pressure trick to sell you here. What the pros actually do when perch get tough — front or no front — is shrink everything and slow it down, and fish an active lure beside a still live-bait rod: flash to draw them, stillness to close them.

weatherOverlays.heading: Calme et brillant
lines: Perch are daylight sight-feeders — they need light to hunt, and bright days are perch days. In spring, sunny afternoons warm the shallows and turn the shallow bite on; that's a real pattern, not a consolation prize.

weatherOverlays.heading: Couvert
lines: The spring rule flips on cloudy days: without sun warming the surface layer, the warm-water-in-the-coves pattern weakens. On grey spring days, check the regular structure instead of chasing warm coves.

weatherOverlays.heading: Venteux
lines: A spring wind pushes the warm surface layer into the coves it blows toward — windward coves can be the warmest water in the lake and hold the fish. Fish the coves the wind is filling.
A spring wind pushes the warm surface layer into the coves it blows toward — windward coves can be the warmest water and hold the fish. Fish the coves the wind is filling.

weatherOverlays.heading: Après la tombée de la nuit
lines: Perch quit at dark — they can hardly see their food below about 2 lux. If it's night, the honest advice is that perch are tomorrow's fish; the last hour of light was their window.
